s1.syndrome_frame: a clinical presentation of respiratory symptoms with a mass in the lung and an expansile lesion in the hyoid bone
salient_findings: a 3.1 × 2.7 × 3.6 cm mass in the right lower lobe
an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone
key_facts: 27-year-old man with a history of melanoma
melanoma was 5 mm‐thick and located on the posterior neck
melanoma was treated six years earlier by wide local excision
no sentinel lymph node biopsy or adjuvant therapy was performed
vital signs were within normal limits
physical examination was notable only for scattered breath sounds without stridor
laboratory studies, including complete blood count and metabolic panel, were unremarkable
endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor
molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation
molecular studies were consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET)
PET/CT showed an FDG-avid right lower lobe mass and an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified hyoid bone lesion
ultrasound–guided core needle biopsy of the hyoid lesion was nondiagnostic

raw.rationale: Molecular studies were consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) and the presence of a malignant small round blue cell tumor in the lung lesion supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: Although molecular studies were consistent with PNET, Ewing sarcoma is a more specific diagnosis that encompasses PNET

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: The presence of a malignant small round blue cell tumor in the lung lesion is not consistent with plasmacytoma

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: The molecular studies and the presence of a malignant small round blue cell tumor in the lung lesion do not support chondrosarcoma

rejected.label: Melanoma metastasis
rejected.why: The molecular studies were consistent with Ewing sarcoma/PNET, and the primary melanoma was treated six years earlier, making metastasis less likely
